critical_code_review_comments: server.py:2074-2089 migrate_master_data is idempotent — safe to restart backend at any time (Brands seeded from products.brand distinct, Territories from user/beat territory strings, Settings from DEFAULT_SETTINGS if missing). Good pattern.

server.py:1825-1828 brand rename cascades update products.brand and schemes.brand in a single update_many; this is not transactional (no session/txn) — if the second update_many fails, products would have new name while schemes still have old. In current MongoDB standalone deployment MongoDB txns aren't available; consider wrapping in try/except with compensating write, or use a single background job with idempotent retry.
server.py:1869-1878 same non-transactional concern for territory rename cascading to users+retailers+beats — three sequential update_many; low risk but worth noting.

server.py:1900 admin retailer edit does not validate salesperson_id (accepts any string). If admin passes a non-existent uuid, retailer becomes orphaned. Consider validating that req.salesperson_id (when provided) matches an existing user with role=salesperson. Same for distributor_id.
server.py:1985-2008 scheme create sets territory=None/distributor_id=None correctly for empty strings via `req.territory or None`; verified by tests. Good.

Admin dashboard salesperson performance table shows leftover TEST users (TEST_User_Renamed EMP43393, EMP43447, TESTSP43385, TESTSP43461) from earlier iterations — cosmetic only; the users are marked active=False by tests but the /api/admin/overview aggregation includes all users regardless of active status. Consider filtering by active=True in the salesperson performance aggregation to hide deactivated test/legacy accounts.

rca_of_issue: No blocking bugs found. Non-blocking: (a) brand/territory rename cascades are non-transactional across collections — acceptable given MongoDB standalone; (b) admin retailer edit doesn't validate salesperson_id/distributor_id existence — low risk since admin has full context; (c) admin salesperson performance aggregation includes inactive users so leftover TEST_* accounts appear in dashboard — cosmetic; (d) no DELETE endpoint for users/brands/territories/schemes/beats — tests use active=False for soft-delete, which is fine but accumulates rows over time.
